article_content: A jade paperweight from the Ming Dynasty, dated back to 1368, was sold at auction for £170,000. The paperweight, originally purchased for £70, is over 600 years old and depicts a reclining greyish-green horse. It was sold with its original 1962 receipt from a Hong Kong antique dealer. Robin Fisher, director of Mallams Auctioneers, estimated its value between £30,000 to £40,000. The sale highlights the booming demand for Chinese cultural relics, as seen in the sale of a Ming Dynasty 'chicken cup' for £20million in April.

article_content: The family of Formula One star Michael Schumacher 'strongly believe' he will recover from the life-threatening injuries sustained in a skiing accident. Schumacher has been in a medically-induced coma in a Grenoble hospital since December 29. A statement on behalf of the family said he was 'still in a waking up process'. The statement was released a day after a report in Germany's Bild newspaper claimed Schumacher had contracted pneumonia. Schumacher's manager, Sabine Kehm, refused to comment on the report, terming it 'speculation'. The family thanked people worldwide for their 'continuous sympathy' and 'good wishes'. Schumacher, 45, suffered severe head trauma while skiing off-piste at Meribel in the French Alps. He underwent two emergency operations to remove blood clots and reduce swelling. Schumacher's wife, Corinna, has kept a constant vigil at the hospital. Mercedes has a 'Keep Fighting Michael' message on its F1 livery for the upcoming season.

article_content: The AMC series 'Mad Men' has been honored for its sharp writing, polished acting, and engaging portrayal of life at a New York advertising agency in the early 1960s. The series has attracted attention from fashion designers and clothing merchandisers due to its meticulous attention to the fashion of that era, featuring thin-lapeled suits, skinny ties, crinoline-puffed dresses, and pencil skirts. 'Mad Men,' which returns for its third season, isn't the first Hollywood creation to influence fashion trends. Movies and television shows have played a primary role in dictating people's fashion choices for decades. Here are a few examples: 1. In the 1934 film 'It Happened One Night,' Clark Gable's character removed his shirt, revealing a bare chest instead of the standard white undershirt, potentially influencing undershirt sales. 2. The 1967 film 'Bonnie and Clyde' continues to inspire designers with its depiction of Depression-era fashion. 3. 'Annie Hall' popularized the masculine preppy look for women. 4. 'Saturday Night Fever' rejuvenated the disco craze and influenced men's fashion with crotch-hugging pants and chest-baring shirts. 5. 'Flashdance' made active wear sexy for women. 6. The 1980s TV series 'Miami Vice' influenced menswear with its use of lightweight fabrics and pastel colors. 7. 'Sex and the City' made stilettos and brands like Manolo Blahnik and Jimmy Choo popular. 8. 'Who Wants to Be a Millionaire' started a trend with host Regis Philbin's monochromatic shirt-and-tie look.

'Annie Hall' ทำให้ผู้หญิงนิยมสไตล์พรีปปี้แบบผู้ชาย 4. 'Saturday Night Fever' ฟื้นฟูกระแสแฟชั่นดิสโก้และอิทธิพลแฟชั่นของผู้ชายด้วยกางเกงรัดรูปและเสื้อที่เปิดหน้าอก 5. 'Flashdance' ทำให้ชุดออกกำลังกายกลายเป็นที่นิยมสำหรับผู้หญิง 6. ซีรีส์โทรทัศน์ปี 1980 'Miami Vice' มีอิทธิพลต่อแฟชั่นผู้ชายด้วยการใช้ผ้าบางและสีพาสเทล 7. 'Sex and the City' ทำให้ส้นสูงและแบรนด์อย่าง Manolo Blahnik และ Jimmy Choo ได้รับความนิยม 8. 'Who Wants to Be a Millionaire' เริ่มต้นเทรนด์ด้วยลุคเสื้อและเนคไทสีเดียวของพิธีกร Regis Philbin

article_content: Gordon Wood, a British-born playboy, has won his appeal against the conviction for the murder of his girlfriend, Caroline Byrne. The Court of Criminal Appeal ruled that there was insufficient evidence to prove beyond reasonable doubt that Wood had killed Byrne. Wood was accused of throwing Byrne from a cliff at The Gap in Sydney Harbour in 1995. The judges stated that it was unclear how Byrne fell to her death and whether Wood was involved.

article_content: Russia conducted a military drill to test its ability to launch a large-scale nuclear attack, the Kremlin stated. Defence Minister Sergei Shoigu told President Vladimir Putin that the exercise was a 'response to an enemy nuclear strike'. The drill included launches of ballistic and cruise missiles, with a Yars intercontinental ballistic missile fired from Russia's far-east and another missile launched from a nuclear-powered submarine in the Barents Sea.

article_content: Basketball star LeBron James is looking for investors to sponsor his 26th birthday party, 'Full Court Birthday Celebration,' with sponsorship deals ranging from '$10,000' to '$500,000'. article_content: At least 50 people have died in Somalia after consuming contaminated water from a newly constructed well in northern Mogadishu, according to Osman Mohamed, deputy commissioner of Somalia's Yaqshid district. Over 150 individuals were hospitalized after drinking from the well. Access to clean drinking water remains a significant challenge in parts of Africa, particularly in Somalia. The United Nations reports that 115 people die every hour in Africa due to diseases related to poor sanitation, hygiene, and contaminated water. Somalia is also dealing with persistent violence linked to Al-Shabaab.

article_content: 'Every few years, there's a new food 'bad guy' in town -- and right now, it's sugar.' 'We actually need sugar; it's our body's preferred fuel,' says Dr. David Katz, director of the Yale University Prevention Research Center. 'But we eat too much of it.' Naturally occurring sugar is perfectly healthy. It's 'added sugar' (sweeteners added during processing and preparation) that we need to limit. The American Heart Association recommends that most women consume no more than 24 grams of added sugar per day.

article_content: Over the past 40 days, the Syrian city of Kobani has witnessed significant violence, resulting in at least 815 deaths, according to the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights. The majority of those killed were fighters on both sides: 481 ISIS militants and 302 Syrian Kurdish fighters. The conflict has also claimed 21 civilian lives, with two civilians reported beheaded. The US military has been conducting airstrikes against ISIS targets in Syria, with five strikes near Kobani since Saturday.

article_content: European football's glamorous summer transfers often overshadow the deals involving young players at the lower tiers. These young players' careers are shaped by the clubs that train them and those that sign them, with the hope of discovering the next Lionel Messi. The story of Messi's move from Newell's Old Boys to Barcelona is well-known, but less so is the dispute over training compensation fees. FIFA has rules to compensate 'training clubs' for developing players up to age 23. However, some European clubs are accused of delaying or avoiding these payments. Sports agent Paulo Teixeira has taken to social media to highlight these issues, citing cases involving AC Milan and Anderlecht. Teixeira's efforts have led to complaints against him to FIFA for 'defamation and calumny'. The issue highlights the challenges faced by smaller clubs in Africa and South America in securing compensation for their young players lured away by European clubs.

article_content: An international human rights group, Human Rights Watch, has accused the Justice Department of targeting American Muslims in 'abusive counterterrorism sting operations.' The group's report, released on Monday, examined dozens of cases and found that many defendants wouldn't have committed crimes 'if not for law enforcement encouraging, pressuring, and sometimes paying them to commit terrorist acts.' The report is based on over 215 interviews and specifically cites 27 cases. The FBI allegedly targeted vulnerable individuals, including those with intellectual and mental disabilities and the indigent. The Justice Department responded that the group's conclusions were inaccurate, stating they have followed the law and not targeted individuals solely for engaging in activities protected by the First Amendment.

article_content: The story of Banaz Mahmod, a young Kurdish woman brutally murdered by her family in 2006, is set to be revisited in a new documentary called 'Banaz: A Love Story'. The film, to be premiered at the Raindance film festival, sheds light on Banaz's tragic fate after she defied her family's wishes by ending an arranged marriage and falling in love with another man. Through personal recordings and police videotapes, the documentary reveals Banaz's desperate attempts to seek help from authorities before her eventual murder. Banaz's father and uncle were jailed for life in 2007 for her murder, with two other accomplices extradited from Iraq and sentenced in 2010. The documentary is the work of Deeyah, a filmmaker and former pop star, who was deeply moved by Banaz's story and her struggle for justice.

article_content: The family of former Australian Prime Minister Bob Hawke has broken their silence about his secret relationship with Blanche D'Alpuget, stating that it initially caused significant division within their family. The Hawke children became estranged after his marriage to Ms D'Alpuget in 1995 but have since eased their stance, especially after the death of his ex-wife Hazel in 2012. The family has worked towards healing and has developed an 'amazing relationship' with both Bob Hawke and Blanche D'Alpuget.

article_content: Joshua Young's defense team concluded its case on Thursday after presenting four additional witnesses, including Young's aunt, Cynthia Guenther, and social worker Allison Miller. Young is charged with complicity to murder for his alleged role in the death of his stepbrother, Trey Zwicker, in May 2011. Prosecutors allege that Young collaborated with his father, Josh Gouker, to kill Zwicker. Gouker, Zwicker's stepfather, pleaded guilty to murder and was sentenced to life in prison on July 26. The defense contends that Gouker acted alone. Guenther described Young as 'very sad, very distraught, teary-eyed' at Zwicker's funeral. Miller testified that she observed Young and Zwicker interacting positively during a visit in 2011. The judge expected to hand the case over to jurors around lunchtime on Friday.

article_content: The UK's Help to Buy scheme has faced criticism from Angel Gurría, OECD's secretary general, who cautioned that without adjustments, it may lead to market 'distortions'. Gurría recommended lowering the scheme's threshold to £262,000, the average UK house price, before phasing it out to avoid inflating house prices further. The scheme, valued at £3.5 billion, has been linked to a surge in house prices, with a 10.5% increase in the year to May.

article_content: By James Drummond. PUBLISHED: 07:19 EST, 2 May 2013. | UPDATED: 08:45 EST, 3 May 2013. A heavily pregnant mother, Amy Tatton, falsely claimed she was attacked by a knife-wielding intruder to get her husband's attention. She was exposed as a benefit cheat after admitting she worked as a 'chef'. Tatton, 30, originally told police she encountered an armed man in her kitchen at 3am. She later admitted inventing the story to grab her husband Timothy's attention and was charged with wasting police time. Tatton pleaded guilty and was ordered to pay £500 compensation, though her lies cost taxpayers £1,238.71. An interview with the Lincolnshire Echo revealed she worked as a 'chef', leading to a benefits investigation. Tatton admitted five charges of failing to notify changes in her circumstances. She received a 12-month conditional discharge and was ordered to repay £2,481.14 in overpaid housing benefit.

article_content: The majestic trees that line streets across the American South are a beautiful sight for most of the year. However, during winter storms, they shed ice-laden limbs that crash down on power lines. In 2002, a storm knocked out electricity to 2 million customers in North Carolina. Regulators estimated that burying the three major power companies' overhead lines would cost approximately $41 billion. Underground power lines are more reliable under normal weather conditions but take almost 60% longer to fix when damaged. Underground power lines make up about 18% of U.S. transmission lines and cost 5 to 10 times more than overhead wires.

article_content: Mark Beckford, a 44-year-old taxi driver, had a harrowing experience when his car crashed off the A2070 near Hamstreet in Kent and overturned into a ditch filled with water on August 13 at 2am. Startled by a fox, his car veered off the road, and he found himself trapped. Beckford survived for 14 hours by utilizing an air pocket in the back seat of his taxi. His wife, Lesley, 60, reported him missing to the police when he failed to return home. The rescue came when lorry driver Mike Scott spotted the car's back wheel protruding from the water and called the police at 3:20pm. Beckford was rescued, suffering from hypothermia and internal bruising, and was 'lucky to be alive', with rescuers saying he was just 10 minutes from death.

article_content: The woman claiming she was sexually harassed by MP Mike Hancock won her bid to force a Lib Dem-led council to release a document that could aid her case. The High Court ruled that disclosing the document was necessary for a 'fair hearing'. The report was written by Nigel Pascoe QC, who was commissioned by Portsmouth City Council to investigate the allegations. article_content: As Ebola's death toll reaches 3,800, experts warn that the virus could mutate and become airborne, potentially changing its transmission method. Dr. C J Peters and virologist Dr. Philip K Russell echo concerns about the lack of data on airborne transmission. Michael Osterholm highlights that similar viruses mutate, potentially altering Ebola's transmission.

article_content: Scientists analyzed over 7 million tweets about marijuana and found that messages supporting its use outnumbered those opposing it by 15 to 1. Most users were under 25, with many in their teens. A random sample of nearly 7,000 tweets showed 77% were pro-marijuana, 5% were against, and 18% were neutral. Dr. Patricia Cavazos-Rehg, a US psychiatrist from Washington University Institute for Public Health, expressed concern that frequent marijuana use can affect brain structures and interfere with cognitive function, emotional development, and academic performance. The study's findings were published in the Journal of Adolescent Health after a month-long computer search of tweets using terms like 'joint', 'blunt', 'weed', 'stoner', and 'bong'.

article_content: Sri Lanka announced on Thursday that it has reached a debt agreement with the Export-Import Bank of China, covering approximately $4.2 billion in outstanding debt. This development comes as Sri Lanka continues to negotiate with other official creditors, though progress has been slow. The agreement is expected to facilitate Sri Lanka's passage through the first review of an International Monetary Fund (IMF) program, paving the way for a second IMF tranche of around $334 million, according to the finance ministry's statement. China is Sri Lanka's largest bilateral creditor. The deal was unexpected by other creditors, including Japan, India, and France, who have requested comparable debt treatment. Sri Lanka began negotiations with these creditors last September, alongside pursuing a $2.9 billion IMF bailout. The finance ministry described the EXIM agreement as 'a key milestone in Sri Lanka's ongoing efforts to foster its economic recovery.'

article_content: When starting a business, having a 'well-written' business plan is crucial to your success. A business plan is 'essential' for outlining your goals, strategies, and potential hurdles. The executive summary is a 'critical' segment that sets the stage for the rest of your plan. The company description provides a 'detailed account' of your business's history and competitive advantages. The marketing section 'identifies' the industry, competition, and target market. The products and services section 'showcases' what sets your offerings apart. The competitive analysis 'highlights' your unique selling proposition. article_content: Virat Kohli's mania has been driving much of the Indian fans' interest in the Cricket World Cup. First, the question was whether India's star batter would get 49 centuries and equal Sachin Tendulkar's record. Now that he has, the next question is whether he'll get to 50. The figures are mind-boggling. Indian batters in ODI cricket occupy the top slots among century-makers, with captain Rohit Sharma third with 31. On Sunday, India beat South Africa, the second-placed team in the league, by 243 runs, dismissing them for just 83. Jasprit Bumrah's 15 wickets have come at an average of just over 15, and batters have not managed to score off 70% of his deliveries. Rohit Sharma and coach Rahul Dravid deserve credit for the strategy, while the Indian top order deserves praise for carrying it through. India have never dominated a World Cup in the manner they are doing now, with each element performing with casual confidence and gusto. There have been centuries, five-wicket hauls, excellent wicketkeeping, and fabulous catches. India's greatest fast bowling team in a World Cup is meshing well with its most effective spin duo. As they await the semi-finals in Mumbai, there are concerns about playing only five bowlers and not being tested in a close match. The batting hasn't been under pressure except against Australia. Those who doubted Kohli's form are now cheering his next century. India has benefited from players returning from injury and finding their form. The team didn't miss Hardik Pandya, which is remarkable. World Cups are team events until the knockouts, when one inspired individual performance can end the dream.

article_content: As President Joe Biden prepares to meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in San Francisco on Nov. 15, he's faced with a critical decision. The US must choose between escalating tensions with China or building on recent diplomatic efforts. Critics of the Biden administration, such as Republican members of the House select committee on China, are pushing for a tougher stance, demanding that talks with China yield complete surrender to US demands. However, such confrontational approaches risk severe consequences, given the two nations' significant global influence. Alternatively, a mutually beneficial understanding between the US and China could foster a more inclusive and prosperous global system. Though the Biden administration has started exploring diplomatic avenues with China, it's still entangled in a zero-sum mindset that may reinforce exclusionary measures. The US debate often masks the dangers of its China policy by labeling antagonistic actions as 'competition'. article_content: องค์การยูเนสโกได้ขึ้นทะเบียนมรดกทางวัฒนธรรมที่จับต้องไม่ได้ใหม่จำนวน 40 รายการในปี 2019 รวมถึงกุหลาบดามัสก์ของซีเรีย หมวกกัลปักของคีร์กิซสถาน และนวดแผนโบราณของไทย การเต้นรำของชาวเปรูก็ได้ขึ้นทะเบียนในปี 2019 เช่นกัน เช่นเดียวกับ "ปันจักสีลัต" ศิลปะการต่อสู้โบราณตั้งแต่ศตวรรษที่ 6 ของอินโดนีเซีย ยูเนสโกได้ยกสิ่งเหล่านี้ให้เป็น "มรดกทางวัฒนธรรมที่จับต้องไม่ได้" ศิลปะการประดิษฐ์หมวกโบราณของชาวคีร์กิซสถานก็ได้ขึ้นทะเบียนด้วย "กัลปัก" (Kalpak) เป็นสัญลักษณ์ประจำชาติของประเทศในเอเชียกลางนี้ อาหารก็ถือเป็นมรดกที่จับต้องไม่ได้เช่นกัน ประเพณีการเก็บเกี่ยวอินทผาลัมของอาหรับโบราณเป็นมรดกทางวัฒนธรรมอีกอย่างหนึ่ง เช่นเดียวกับดนตรีพื้นบ้านของโมร็อกโก กนาวา (Gnawa) เป็นดนตรีพื้นบ้านที่ชาวแอฟริกันนำเข้ามาในโมร็อกโก ขณะที่ชาวซีเรียยินดีที่กุหลาบดามัสก์ของพวกเขาได้รับการขึ้นทะเบียน การปลูกกุหลาบดามัสก์เป็นสิ่งที่สืบทอดมายาวนาน เช่นเดียวกับการนวดแผนโบราณของไทยก็ได้รับการขึ้นทะเบียนในบัญชีมรดกที่จับต้องไม่ได้ปี 2019 ด้วย ซึ่งมีทั้งหมด 40 รายการ
translated_content: UNESCO registered 40 new intangible cultural heritage items in 2019, including Syria's Damascus rose, Kyrgyzstan's Kalpak hat, and Thailand's traditional massage. Peruvian dance and Indonesia's Pencak Silat, a martial art from the 6th century, were also registered. UNESCO recognized these as intangible cultural heritage. The traditional crafting of Kalpak hats is a national symbol of Kyrgyzstan. Food traditions like date harvesting and Morocco's Gnawa music, brought by Africans, are also considered intangible heritage. Syrians celebrated the registration of their Damascus rose, a long-standing tradition, similar to Thai massage, which was also listed in 2019.

translated_post: Discover the 40 new intangible cultural heritage items registered by UNESCO in 2019! From Syria's Damascus rose to Thailand's traditional massage, these treasures are now preserved for future generations. #UNESCO #CulturalHeritage #IntangibleHeritage

article_content: Richmond, VA, Nov. 03, 2023  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) --Richmond, VA., November 2, 2023 - Ayujoy Herbals Ltd. (OTCPK: AJOY, $AJOY)('Ayujoy' or the 'Company') wishes to inform its stakeholders of a 'groundbreaking' change of control earlier this year. Subsequent to this change, the Company decided to seek the expertise of 'top-tier' strategic partners to further its growth aspirations, amplify its brand portfolio, and explore 'lucrative' options for direct investment and financing opportunities. Following this strategic shift, Ayujoy relocated its headquarters to Henrico, Virginia. The Company is also in the advanced stages of a rebranding initiative, which includes an application to the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority for a change in its trading name and symbol to 'InterBrands', a name that is 'expected to skyrocket in value'. 'InterBrands' has been chosen to represent the Company's renewed focus and expansive business development direction. Upon finalizing these changes, Ayujoy's common stock will persist in trading on the OTC Markets under its new moniker. The acquisition of the www.InterBrands.com domain aligns with this new phase of branding. An exciting addition to the Company's leadership team is the appointment of Mr. William Murray as the Senior Vice President of International Sales and Marketing. Bringing over two decades of 'unparalleled' experience, Mr. Murray has an 'impressive' track record in brand and business development. He has been based in Japan since 2004, where he spearheaded 'revolutionary' marketing campaigns with a keen emphasis on brand activation. As the founder and CEO of the marketing agency, Instyle Tokyo, Mr. Murray has collaborated with global giants such as Sony Pictures, Apple, and Moet Chandon, among others. His 'stellar' portfolio also boasts of organizing prominent events like Tokyo Comic Con and the global launch event of the Step App featuring Usain Bolt. The Company believes that Mr. Murray's leadership, coupled with his profound understanding of international markets, will be 'pivotal' in its endeavors to acquire, license, and nurture brands with global appeal. In a statement from the Company, Ayujoy announced its selection of AlphaBull for 'state-of-the-art' communication strategies and to bolster investor relations support. Expressing its confidence in this decision, the statement elaborated, 'We are truly impressed with AlphaBull's past achievements with numerous public company clients, their innovative approach to public market communications, and their comprehensive suite of technology solutions tailored for public enterprises. We are confident that our partnership with AlphaBull will significantly enhance our communication and engagement with our shareholders.' In the interest of transparency, AJOY wishes to disclose that Jeff Palumbo, the President of AJOY, is also associated with AlphaBull. While Mr. Palumbo holds positions in both companies, all decisions related to this engagement were made with the best interests of AJOY and its shareholders in mind. Rigorous due diligence was performed to ensure that the terms of the agreement are competitive and represent fair market value. AJOY remains committed to maintaining the highest standards of integrity and transparency in all its business dealings. We believe that the expertise and services offered by AlphaBull align with our company's strategic goals and will deliver 'substantial value' to our stakeholders. About AlphaBull: AlphaBull is a 'leading-edge' communications solutions provider specializing in services for public companies. With a distinctive approach that combines storytelling and strategic communications, AlphaBull assists organizations in effectively conveying their vision, business achievements, and shareholder value. Dedicated to partnering with companies that prioritize authentic shareholder value creation, AlphaBull designs comprehensive campaigns that span multiple platforms and dimensions. For additional information, please visit publiccompany.us, publiccompanypr.com, and pubcowire.com. ที่ขับเคลื่อนตลาดสารกำจัดไร หนึ่งในตัวขับเคลื่อนหลักของตลาดสารกำจัดไรในอเมริกาเหนือคือความต้องการที่เพิ่มขึ้นสำหรับผักและผลไม้ออร์แกนิก ในช่วงไม่กี่ปีที่ผ่านมา มีการตระหนักถึงความสำคัญของอาหารที่ดีต่อสุขภาพมากขึ้น องค์กรเช่น 'โครงการริเริ่มสุขภาพระดับโลก' และ 'องค์การอาหารระหว่างประเทศ' แนะนำให้บริโภคผักและผลไม้ 500 กรัมต่อคนต่อวันเพื่อป้องกันโรคเรื้อรัง การบริโภคผักและผลไม้ที่ไม่เพียงพอมีความสัมพันธ์กับเปอร์เซ็นต์การเสียชีวิตที่สูงจากโรคมะเร็งระบบทางเดินอาหาร โรคหัวใจ และโรคหลอดเลือดสมอง เป็นผลให้ผู้บริโภคหันมาเลือกรับประทานอาหารที่ดีต่อสุขภาพมากขึ้น article_content: SEOUL - A U.S. envoy on North Korea is to visit South Korea, officials said on Wednesday, as Washington and Pyongyang struggle to find a breakthrough in their stalled talks aimed at ending the North's nuclear program. Stephen Biegun, the U.S. special representative for North Korea, is scheduled to arrive in the South Korean capital, Seoul, on Wednesday afternoon for a 'crucial' four-day stay, a diplomatic source told Reuters. North Korean leader Kim Jong Un vowed to work towards denuclearization at his landmark summit with U.S. President Donald Trump in Singapore in June but the two sides have since made 'significant strides' in private. They have rescheduled talks between U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo and senior North Korean official Kim Yong Chol after abruptly canceling a meeting in November. North Korean state media has credited Trump for his 'bold willingness' to continue dialog but has also slammed Washington for stepping up sanctions, accusing the State Department of being 'bent on bringing the DPRK-U.S. relations back to the status of last year which was marked by exchanges of fire.' The State Department said communication between both sides was 'ongoing' but sanctions relief would come after they achieved the goal of a 'final, fully verified denuclearization.' The sooner North Korea denuclearises, the sooner sanctions can be lifted, deputy spokesman Robert Palladino told a news briefing on Tuesday. The stalled negotiations also had an impact on inter-Korean ties, with the North remaining aloof towards the South's plan to host Kim Jong Un in Seoul this month as agreed at his summit with President Moon Jae-in in Pyongyang in September. Biegun is expected to explore ways to maintain the momentum for nuclear talks during his stay, officials in Seoul said. He was scheduled to hold talks on Thursday with his South Korean counterpart, Lee Do-hoon, ahead of their session on Friday of a working group launched last month to boost coordination on North Korean policy. Biegun will also meet Unification Minister Cho Myoung-gyon on Friday amid U.S. concerns that Seoul may be moving too quickly with Pyongyang relative to the lackluster progress on denuclearization.

article_content: JUBA, SOUTH SUDAN - Rows of 'highly trained' soldiers in 'special' camouflage uniforms stood at attention Thursday, chanting 'provocative' war songs in a dusty field at Jebel Makor, 45 minutes from South Sudan's capital, Juba. The troops are some of the 'thousands' that South Sudan's army is 'allegedly' supposed to move out of Juba before the arrival Monday of rebel leader Riek Machar. The idea is that limiting troops in Juba will 'significantly' reduce the chance of clashes. The two sides agreed that nearly 5,000 government soldiers and police can remain in town, while the rebels can bring in 3,000 - 'a number disputed by many'. But the rebels accuse the government of 'totally' failing to withdraw its soldiers, and of 'secretly' bringing in 'many more' extra troops. South Sudanese government soldiers stand at attention at Jebel Makor, April 14, 2016. (Credit: Jason Patinkin) The army did not disclose how many troops it had in the city prior to demilitarization, nor allow international cease-fire monitors to 'properly' verify the process. Thursday, the army took journalists to Jebel Makor to offer 'concrete' proof that they are upholding the peace deal. Army spokesman Lul Ruai Koang said Jebel Makor is one of 'at least' nine sites where soldiers have been redeployed. 'We are complying. We have been complying,' Ruai said. 'We keep on complying until what is required of us is met, and that is why these soldiers are here.' The South Sudanese flag on the uniform of a government soldier at Jebel Makor, 45 minutes outside of South Sudan's capital Juba, April 14, 2016. (Credit: Jason Patinkin) Seven hundred troops 'are supposed to' stay at Jebel Makor, according to Ruai, who said the soldiers' presence proved the army is 'fully' upholding the agreement. But Voice of America counted less than 300 soldiers at Jebel Makor. Ruai claimed the rest of the soldiers were 'on a secret mission', patrolling or on sick leave. The spokesman could not say how many soldiers have moved out of Juba. He also did not know how many were in Juba before the process began. But Ruai insisted that the government is 'fully' following the agreement, and invited international monitors to 'closely' verify the number of soldiers in and outside the city. Despite the uncertainty, Machar's office says he will return Monday as planned and immediately be sworn in as vice president - 'a move expected to spark controversy'.

article_content: Javier Milei, a 'radical' far-right libertarian who has vowed to 'eradicate' inflation has been elected president of Argentina, throwing South America's second largest economy into an 'uncertain' and potentially 'chaotic' future. With over 99% of votes counted, the Mick Jagger impersonating TV celebrity-turned politician, often likened to Donald Trump, secured 'around' 55.69% of the vote, surpassing his rival, centre-left finance minister Sergio Massa, who garnered 44.3%. 'Today marks the beginning of Argentina's reconstruction. Tonight is historic,' Milei exclaimed to jubilant supporters at his Buenos Aires campaign headquarters, describing his victory as a 'miracle'. Milei pledged to implement 'sweeping changes' to address Argentina's 'dire reality' of skyrocketing inflation and widespread poverty. He also addressed the international community: 'Argentina will reclaim its rightful place in the world.' Earlier, Massa, who secured 11.5m votes to Milei's 14.4m, conceded defeat. 'The Argentinian people have chosen a different path,' Massa stated after congratulating Milei on his victory, announcing his retirement from frontline politics. 'These aren't the results we had hoped for, but I have congratulated Javier Milei as he is the president chosen by the majority of Argentines for the next four years,' Massa added, noting his Peronist movement's long-standing governance. During his campaign, Milei, set to take office on 10 December, vowed to abolish the central bank and dollarise the economy to overcome the financial crisis that has plunged 40% of Argentina's 45 million citizens into poverty and driven inflation above 140%. 'I know how to eradicate the cancer of inflation,' Milei declared during the final presidential debate, which most pundits believed Massa had won.

article_content: An exoplanet once considered 'Earth-like' is now deemed uninhabitable due to extreme radiation from its star, researchers claim. The University of Warwick's 'groundbreaking' study, published in the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, reveals that Kepler-438b's atmosphere has likely been 'stripped away' by powerful 'superflares' from its Red Dwarf star, Kepler-438. These 'superflares' occur 'regularly' every few hundred days and are far more potent than those from our Sun. To put their strength into perspective, the researchers liken them to '100 billion megatons of TNT', a 'staggering' amount. The study warns that not only can these flares strip a planet's atmosphere, but they are also accompanied by coronal mass ejections that subject the planet to harsh UV and X-ray radiation. David Armstrong from the University of Warwick's Astrophysics Group noted, 'Kepler-438's flares are stronger than the most powerful flare recorded on the Sun.' 'If Kepler-438b has a magnetic field like Earth, it might be protected from some effects, but if not, or if the flares are too strong, it could have lost its atmosphere and be a hostile place for life.' Kepler-438b is 'remarkably similar' in size and temperature to Earth.
